decisions.rationale: SQLAlchemy's async layer needs greenlet at runtime and does not install it by default; a clean checkout installed fine then failed on the first async connection.
decisions.test_implication: Assert the declared deps include the asyncio extra or greenlet, and that a clean venv can run alembic.

decisions.summary: Deferred migration moved to migrations/deferred/ with its own ini - FINDING-2.5
decisions.rationale: The deferral was a docstring, and Alembic does not read docstrings: 0002 was the chain head, so plain `alembic upgrade head` built both hnsw indexes on empty tables. Location is a mechanism; prose is not. Also fixed: Alembic 1.18 replaced version_path_separator with path_separator, without which version_locations parsed as one path.
decisions.tradeoff: Two ini files. The asymmetry is deliberate - the dangerous path must be chosen.
decisions.test_implication: `alembic upgrade head` applies zero hnsw indexes; `alembic -c alembic.deferred.ini upgrade head` applies exactly two, both vector_cosine_ops.

decisions.rationale: Empty output, max_tokens truncation, and missing source URLs all fail while nothing raises, and all are unrecoverable once persisted because the next run's period_start moves past the window. The URL check is INV-10 in code.
decisions.tradeoff: A bad week costs one Sonnet call and an empty inbox instead of a plausible-looking digest.
decisions.test_implication: Test the four rejection cases directly, and assert a rejected digest writes NO row, NO file, and attempts NO send.

decisions.rationale: Ranking twice meant score_clusters running in between could change the answer, so the digests row would archive a different set of clusters than its prose describes, with nothing to reveal the mismatch.
decisions.tradeoff: The scalar-string return is still tolerated for hand-assembled prompts.
decisions.test_implication: Assert the persisted cluster_ids come from the same ranking that built the prompt, even when a later ranking would differ.

decisions.summary: Batch id logged at ERROR if its tracking row fails - FINDING-2.9
decisions.rationale: Between API acceptance and the row committing, the batch is billed but unknown to the system. Losing that window orphans the results AND causes the next tick to re-submit the same posts.
decisions.tradeoff: The exception still propagates; the log line is the only recovery path.
decisions.test_implication: Assert the accepted batch id appears in the ERROR log and the exception still raises.

decisions.summary: Three nested failure domains in Reddit ingest - FINDING-2.11
decisions.rationale: Cycle 2 isolated failures per target and stopped there, so one bad submission still discarded every row already collected from that subreddit.
decisions.tradeoff: Broad `except Exception` around third-party attribute access; every one logs at WARNING with subreddit and id.
decisions.test_implication: A failing submission, a failing comment tree, and a listing that raises mid-iteration must each preserve rows collected before them.

decisions.summary: _parse_created_at returns None instead of raising - FINDING-2.10
decisions.rationale: The old expression raised KeyError / AttributeError / TypeError depending on how the field was malformed, and each escaped ingest_hn_query and discarded the whole page.
decisions.tradeoff: A malformed hit is dropped silently apart from a WARNING.
decisions.test_implication: Missing / null / numeric / unparseable inputs return None; a naive timestamp comes back UTC-attached rather than dropped.

decisions.summary: DELETE FROM clusters, not TRUNCATE - FINDING-2.12
decisions.rationale: Postgres refuses to TRUNCATE a table referenced by a foreign key even when no referencing rows exist - the check is on the constraint, not the data. TRUNCATE CASCADE would have worked and would also have destroyed every embedding the rebuild exists to reuse.
decisions.tradeoff: Slower. Cluster ids are deliberately not restarted so old digests' cluster_ids cannot point at unrelated rows.
decisions.test_implication: recluster_all against live Postgres: the FK case, and that embeddings survive.

decisions.summary: Compose ports bound to loopback - FINDING-2.13
decisions.rationale: A bare 5432:5432 publishes on every interface, exposing scraped post bodies and author names behind the password 'postgres', plus a Redis with no password.
decisions.tradeoff: Remote access now needs an explicit tunnel.
decisions.test_implication: Assert both published ports carry the 127.0.0.1 prefix.

decisions.summary: resolve_log_level falls back to INFO - FINDING-2.14
decisions.rationale: basicConfig(level='not-a-level') raises inside on_startup, so one typo in .env stops the worker booting. Logging is diagnostics and must never take the pipeline down.
decisions.tradeoff: An invalid level is silently INFO rather than loud.
decisions.test_implication: Padding, case, unknown names, numeric strings.

findings.detail: Migration 0001, raw-SQL constraints, idempotent upsert, vertical ranking, and both halves of the INV-2 partition witness pass on PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector 0.8.5.
ARQ ctx signatures, enrichment cross-field validation and partial collection, pending-batch guard, and narrowed pure-function AST checks pass.
Filter reasons and gates, scoring behavior, ordinary timestamp/author handling, HTML stripping, and dedupe pass.
Clean declared install cannot run Alembic because greenlet or sqlalchemy[asyncio] is not declared.
0002 is the Alembic head; live alembic upgrade head applies both HNSW indexes despite the decision calling the migration deferred.
Digest prose with a quote but no source URL is persisted.
No-text and max_tokens-truncated model responses are persisted as complete digests.
The prompt and persisted cluster_ids come from two independent ranking queries and can disagree.
If tracking persistence fails after Anthropic accepts a batch, the recoverable batch ID is neither persisted nor logged.
A missing, malformed, or non-string created_at aborts the HN query and loses partial progress.
One submission or comment-expansion error aborts its subreddit and discards later submissions.
Live PostgreSQL rejects recluster_all's TRUNCATE because enriched_signals references clusters.
PostgreSQL and Redis publish default ports on all interfaces instead of loopback.
An unknown or whitespace-padded LOG_LEVEL raises ValueError during worker startup.

open_blockers.detail: test_hnsw_migration_uses_cosine_operator_class and test_deferred_hnsw_migration_is_not_alembic_head cannot both pass. The first reads migrations/versions/0002_hnsw_indexes.py by hard-coded path; the second requires Alembic's head to be 0001. Alembic loads every .py in a scanned version location and raises CommandError on any lacking a `revision` attribute, and it does not recurse into subdirectories - so a revision file in versions/ is necessarily in the chain and necessarily the head. FINDING-2.5 is fixed; the path assertion must follow the file to migrations/deferred/0002_hnsw_indexes.py. Not edited by the Builder: Validator-owned file.
Manual LLM and digest quality criteria have no assertion form. Unchanged since cycle 1 and still the criteria that actually decide whether the system works.
